title: Guard the repository root against stray binaries and scratch files
description:
Nothing stops the next live test from committing another hello.txt, and tk.exe has been sitting untracked in the working tree.

Add a Go test that reads the repository root and fails on any tracked file matching a stray-artifact shape: *.exe, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib, and scratch names (hello.txt, goodbye.txt, test.txt, tmp.*). Keep the list short and explicit rather than clever - a guard nobody can read is a guard nobody keeps.

The test must name the offending file and say why it is refused. Do NOT delete hello.txt or goodbye.txt here; a sibling tick does that. Write the test so it passes once they are gone.
acceptance_criteria: The new test fails on a planted root-level stray.exe and passes on a clean root, and go test -short -count=1 ./... passes
